title: Rapid decision heuristics for SE accounts - draft
content:
Context / purpose:
This is a compact, practical cheat-sheet for field SEs to make fast decisions during qualification and discovery. Focus: when to recommend Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private, when to push quantization/throughput tradeoffs, and how to configure canaries and fallbacks under pressure.

Status: rough draft — meant for rapid iteration. Use freely in calls; please flag contradictions with the Dedicated pricing team (Evan) and product constraints (Lena).

Top-level guidance (30s elevator):
- If customer values time-to-market and has moderate PII: start with Hosted API, propose a migration path to Dedicated once steady throughput > 2M tokens/mo or latency SLOs are <150ms p99.
- If regulatory / VPC / on-prem required: Private deployment. Recommend early infra kickstart call (solutions-eng).
- If customer needs predictable unit economics and dedicated SLAs: Dedicated with reserved capacity + burst policy.

Quick qualification checklist (v1):
- Data sensitivity: public / internal / regulated? (If regulated -> Private)
- Peak queries per second and expected steady QPS (if >200 qps sustained -> Dedicated)
- P99 latency requirement (if <= 150ms and high throughput -> Dedicated or Dedicated + optimized model)
- Cost sensitivity: absolute monthly budget vs. cost per 1M tokens
- Integration timeline: weeks -> Hosted API; months + infra alignment -> Dedicated/Private

Heuristics for recommending model variants and runtime knobs:
- Latency-first (low-tolerance p99): Recommend smaller LLM variant + aggressive batching disabled + real-time KV cache enablement. Consider lower top_p / stop sequences.
- Quality-first (few-shot, long context): Recommend larger model family, suggest embedding + retrieval caching; warn on cost.
- Cost-first (high volume, low/medium quality needs): Recommend quantized model variant + continuous batching + prefix caching. Estimate cost delta with quick back-of-envelope.

Canary & fallback quick recipe (field checklist):
1) Canary plan (initial 2 weeks): 5% traffic -> targeted SE route, measure latency/cost/quality on 10k calls. Track: p50/p95/p99 latency, token per call, top-1 quality score against sample prompts.
2) Roll decision: If quality delta < 3% and p99 meets SLO -> expand to 30% next week. If not, rollback and route to fallback.
3) Fallback policy: define primary model, cheaper fallback variant, and region fallback. Pre-configure routing policy in Console before canary.

Sample one-line field scripts to use in call:
- "To get you live fastest, we can onboard on Hosted API and run a 2-week canary with a deterministic rollback policy. If throughput grows we’ll plan a Dedicated onboarding with predictable SLOs."
- "If you need private control plane and HSM keys, we’ll schedule a Private deployment scoping call. Timeline normally 6-10 weeks for infra and compliance."

Technical quick wins to propose (10–20 min handoff items):
- Turn on prefix/KV caching for chat-heavy flows (estimate: 30–50% token savings for repeated context).
- Use embeddings + reranker for long-document retrieval to drop per-request tokens.
- Enable batching for async pathways; keep interactive endpoints unbatched or lower batch sizes.

Common objections + suggested responses (short):
- "Your hosted API is too expensive": "We can run a short economics model: baseline current cost X, projected token volume, and show savings via caching + quantization. If steady load, Dedicated pricing often beats hosted for committed volumes."
- "We need on-prem due to compliance": "Private is designed for this; we’ll scope network and KMS requirements. In many cases a VPC private deployment is faster than full on-prem."
- "We need 99ms p99": "We’ll assess model size + run a latency profile; if requirements bind, Dedicated with regional placement and kernel selection is the path."

Open questions to resolve with Product / Pricing (tag for action):
- How low can we push Dedicated reserved commit for startups (pricing floor)? (owner: Evan)
- Exact KV cache savings signal to show in SE demo console (owner: Lena)
- Simple cost calc widget we can run during demo (owner: Samir / growth eng)

Playbook snippets (copy/paste for internal use):
- On call: "Let’s agree on a 2-week sample set of 2000 representative requests. We’ll run them against Hosted API and the candidate Dedicated config so you can see end-to-end latency and cost comparisons."
- Email follow-up template (post-demo):
  Subject: Next steps & quick economics from today
  Body: Hi <Name>, great conversation today. Attached are the test plan, the 2-week canary steps, and a first-pass cost comparison. If you’d like, we’ll spin up a Dedicated proof-of-concept and demo the canary metrics mid-week next week.

Call-out: quick tables to build for the SE dashboard (todo) - backlog:
- 3-row summary: Hosted / Dedicated / Private with bullets (time-to-live, cost profile, compliance fit).
- Canary metrics snapshot mockup (p50/p95/p99, tokens per call, quality sample)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Draft 1-pager for Legal on Private deployment SLAs (Samir to start).
- Add explicit migration checklist from Hosted -> Dedicated (include infra steps, data transfer notes).
- Create short demo script that shows cost delta with caching on/off (need synthetic dataset).

Slack trails & refs:
- See thread: #se-handbook-thread-593 for earlier experiments and sample prompts.
- Demo artifacts live in GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/278 (WIP slides + screenshots).

End — please add edits inline. If you’re an SE and used this on a call, add a short note of the outcome at the top (one sentence).

Unresolved: decide if we should recommend a minimum committed token volume threshold for Dedicated in SE playbook (proposal: 2M tokens/mo). Will confirm with pricing.
plain_text_preview: Compact heuristics for SEs to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private + canary/fallback checklist. Draft; action items for Pricing/Product included.
